summary: L-4 cab on Bear Creek Mountain in the Goat Rocks Wilderness, built early 1930s, last staffed 1945, gone by 1960; no source describes remains.

facts.status_note: Gone by 1960 per the register and two other lists; no source found describes what remains at the summit

access.note: Reached by a Forest Service trail inside Goat Rocks Wilderness; a free wilderness permit is filled out at the trailhead. No closure found in the pages read

visit.drive_up: Roads are good until the last half mile, where some high clearance is best (WillhiteWeb, undated)
visit.trail_note: Forest Service lists the Bear Creek Mountain Lookout Trail (1130 A), reached from the Section 3 Lake or Conrad Meadows trailheads. The trail is in Goat Rocks Wilderness and is not recommended for horses.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Wenatchee National Forest per firelookout.com)

events.note: Sources say the L-4 cab was built in the early 1930s; 1930 is used as the start of that decade
Panorama photos taken from the site on July 24, 1934
Last staffed in 1945 per the register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb
Sources say 'gone by 1960' and do not say how the cab left the summit
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on July 19, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Washington lookouts list says 'Removed' with no date, while the other lists say the cab was gone by 1960. These do not conflict on the date, and the story uses the 1960 date. No source says whether the cab was removed or destroyed.

notes_for_editor: Brief access was 'unknown'; set to public with a permit based on the Forest Service trail page. Built year 1930 is a decade placeholder for 'early 1930s'. The register and firelookout.com share wording, so they are not independent. No source describes remains at the summit. Willhite's road notes are undated.
